hotspot_events.title: Section 338 Canada list adds window air conditioners and other HVAC categories with additional 50% tariff (effective Oct 30); 178 Section 301 exclusions enter 6-day countdown to Nov 09 expiration with no extension yet
hotspot_events.heat_reason: The newly finalized policy directly hits window air conditioners and iron/steel valves with a 50% tariff hike, combined with a 6-day action window for Section 301 exclusions; dual tariff checks must be completed within this week for customs declaration.
hotspot_events.summary: On Oct 23, Trump signed a revised proclamation (amending Proclamation 11048), subjecting 100 tariff lines including window air conditioners and iron/steel valves (8481.80.30) to a 50% Section 338 tariff starting Oct 30 at 0:01 EDT (no exemption for USMCA origin, stackable with Section 232; 22 tariff lines removed). Meanwhile, 178 Section 301 exclusions will expire on Nov 09 (EDT); as of Nov 03, USTR has not issued an extension notice. Upon expiration, List 1~3 tariffs will revert to 25% and List 4A to 7.5%.

hotspot_events.title: Shengyi raises laminate prices again by 15%/25% in November (largest single-round hike in nearly two years); Panasonic to hike multilayer PCB substrates by 200% from 2027-01
hotspot_events.heat_reason: A new round of CCL price increases lands in November; Shengyi's order book is full through 2027-01, with FR-4 lead times extended to 4 weeks, putting immediate cost pressure on drive boards and controllers.
hotspot_events.summary: Shengyi Technology will raise prices on M6 and below laminates by 15% and prepreg (PP) by 25% in November, marking the largest single-round increase in nearly two years (standard FR-4 cumulative increase reached 130% within the year); orders are fully scheduled through 2027-01. Panasonic notified that some multilayer PCB substrate prices will be raised by 200% starting from 2027-01. About 30% of global copper-clad laminate (CCL) capacity has shifted to high-end AI products, squeezing the supply of standard laminates.
